correctness.rationale: Braunfeld’s full product has coordinate equivalence relations and quotient orders, forcing the automorphism group to act coordinatewise as Aut(Q,<)^d. Tuple orbits are therefore d weak orders. Injectivity is exactly absence of a pair tied in every coordinate. The exact profiles follow by Stirling inversion. For d>=3, one prescribed collision has probability (F_{n-1}/F_n)^d and two distinct collision events have probability (F_{n-2}/F_n)^d; first and second Bonferroni bounds plus F_{n-1}/F_n~(log 2)/n prove the stated first deficit term. The finite verifier independently enumerates weak-order powers in small arities and matches the formulas.

value.rationale: The result places a clean probabilistic threshold on a canonical homogeneous family: one coordinate is overwhelmingly noninjective, two coordinates retain a nontrivial limiting collision mass, and three or more coordinates become asymptotically injective with an explicit first deficit term. It also explains the classical incidence-matrix constant as the critical member of a model-theoretic product family.
